metadata.case_name: LEUNG SAI-KUI AND ANOTHER v. F. ZIMMERN & CO. (A FIRM)

injuries.description: A clinical diagnosis of right cerebral contusion was made
source: A clinical diagnosis of right cerebral contusion was made
On 14.1.76, a right temporoparietal craniotomy was done with a spiration of right intracerebral haemstoma.

injuries.description: x-ray of lumbar spine revealed a compression fracture of L1 vertabra
source: x-ray of lumbar spine revealed a compression fracture of L1 vertabra.
As a result of this injury the plaintiff had residual left hemiplegia and post traumatic epilepsy which was controlled with anticonvulsant.
As a result of this injury the plaintiff had residual left hemiplegia and post traumatic epilepsy which was controlled with anticonvulsant.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: upper motor neurone type of left facial palsy
source: There was upper motor neurone type of left facial palsy and left hemiparesis with left extensor plantar response.

injuries.description: severe visual disability in both eyes following injuries received in the accident on December 28, 1975
source: there is no doubt in his mind that the plaintiff had suffered a severe visual disability in both eyes following injuries received in the accident on December 28, 1975.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of eye or orbit, unspecified

injuries.description: left homonymous hemianopia which is a loss of vision on the left side of each eye
source: the plaintiff also suffers from left homonymous hemianopia which is a loss of vision on the left side of each eye.

injuries.description: infarction involving right anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries territories
source: A C. T. brain scan showed infarction involving right anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries territories.

injuries.description: a 1" laceration at the left occipital region
source: There was periorbital swelling over the right eye and a 1" laceration at the left occipital region.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

manifestations.description: drowsy but responded to simple commands
left hemiparesis with left extensor plantar response
attacks of left sided convulsions
incontinence of urine and faeces, initially
fits of violence
mild left side headache associated with vertigo
very spastic left limbs with marked clonus
could just manage to walk about in his quarters with the help of a stick
after 2nd November 1983: way of talking had deteriorated, very slow and drowsy; walking impossible as limbs very weak
slurred voice, response very slow; further conversation unintelligible
claimed that he was not able to see well and made mistakes in counting fingers placed 3 feet from him
right eye could not move towards the left side
right hand strong but movements clumsy; right leg clumsy
left arm and left hand very stiff and no voluntary movement possible; left leg stiff but able to kick out when asked
tube connecting his penis to a receptacle as he was not able to control his bowel and his bladder
vision: could see from a distance of two feet, one or two fingers on both eyes
face expressionless; did not have a normal facial expression
Vestibular Nerve disturbed causing giddiness
tongue could protrude towards the left side but difficulty protruding to the right side
cannot walk due to loss of control of his left leg; flexion contracture of his left elbow
wasting of right limbs due to lack of use over the years
speech incomprehensible except to those who spend a long time in his company; communication limited to indicating basic needs and desires
sexual intercourse between the plaintiff and his wife has not taken place since the accident

treatments_received: right temporoparietal craniotomy with a spiration of right intracerebral haemstoma
nursing care (registered nurse 8 hours per day)
treatments_future: registered nurse care 8 hours per day

losses.description: Partial tetraplegic: left side hemiplegic and right side wasted; loss of most of his teeth noted in evidence
Severe visual disability in both eyes; left homonymous hemianopia
Cannot perform any function for himself; requires full time care and attention either at home or in an institution for the rest of his life

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Inability to feed himself; requires assistance for washing and other personal care
Speech incomprehensible except to those who spend a long time in his company; slurred speech and limited communication

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Sexual intercourse between the plaintiff and his wife has not taken place since the accident
Unable to walk; requires wheelchair and walking aids previously
